rollups.text: Crystal’s family movie-marathon planning evolved from a planned April 6–7, 2024 weekend to a reported completed marathon. On March 12, Crystal planned a marathon for April 6–7, initially targeting five family-friendly films and later choosing a five-film list; she also set a March 25 watchlist-finalization target. On March 12, she later stated a March 28 deadline, and on March 28 she finalized an eight-film list: Soul, Paddington 2, The Mitchells vs. The Machines, Coco, Moana, Zootopia, Tangled, and The Secret Life of Pets. Paddington 2 was rented; Crystal later reported saving $3.99 by renting it rather than subscribing. On April 6–7, the marathon was planned with family members, including Amy and Kyle; Mason was expected at noon on April 7, so Crystal shifted that day’s start from 1:00 PM to 12:30 PM. On April 6, Crystal reported the family completed the planned movies despite Francis’s nap being delayed by two hours. On April 8, she said the family had completed eight selected movies over the weekend. The conversation contains several conflicting assistant-proposed schedules, which were not all confirmed by Crystal.

Crystal planned a May 11–12, 2024 family movie marathon. On April 30, she sent Lily’s parents formal WhatsApp invitations; they confirmed attendance on May 1. On May 3, Crystal sent a schedule and information about snacks, activities, supervision, and a request to disclose allergies or dietary restrictions and reconfirm attendance. Amy’s evening church service led Crystal to set a 2:00 PM start on May 11, and Crystal confirmed Encanto for that start time. The schedule sent to Lily’s parents listed Encanto, Turning Red, Onward, and The Princess Bride on May 11, with a babysitter caring for Francis during The Princess Bride, and Strange World, The One and Only Ivan, and Coco on May 12. Other lineups and activities were proposed but not confirmed. By May 11, Crystal described the marathon as having started at 2:00 PM and ended at 9:00 PM; on May 15, she reported that the family had watched 15 family movies in six weeks, exceeding its initial goal by 50%.

Crystal’s internet plan and streaming experience changed over time. On May 3, 2024, she and her family had a 100 Mbps plan and were considering an upgrade to 200 Mbps for an additional $20 per month, but postponed the decision. On May 15, one record says Crystal had upgraded to 200 Mbps for $20 per month and that streaming improved and buffering fell by 75%; a separate record that day says she had never upgraded and was still considering the change. The records therefore conflict about whether the upgrade had occurred.

Films Crystal’s family was reported to have watched or selected, with dates: Forrest Gump (selected for a planned movie night with Thomas and college friends, 2024-03-12); The Incredibles, Finding Nemo, Coco, Paddington, and Trolls (selected for family movie night, 2024-03-12); Soul, Paddington 2, The Mitchells vs. The Machines, Coco, Moana, Zootopia, Tangled, and The Secret Life of Pets (finalized marathon list, 2024-03-28); Moana and Zootopia (approved April 8 movie-day schedule, 2024-04-08); Encanto (chosen for family movie night, 2024-05-03; confirmed for 2:00 PM on 2024-05-11). Crystal later reported Michelle liked Coco and Francis enjoyed Paddington 2 (2024-04-08), and that the family had watched Coco and Paddington 2 (2024-05-03).

rollups.text: Recurring family movie snacks and contributions, with dates: popcorn, candy, chips and crackers, fruit and vegetables, and drinks were suggested for the March 2024 movie weekend (2024-03-12); Crystal planned themed cupcakes from The Sweet Spot and raised the snack budget to $65 (2024-03-28); Emily offered homemade popcorn seasoning, and Crystal later said the family used Emily’s recipe (offered 2024-03-28; used by 2024-04-08); Crystal ordered 24 cupcakes from The Sweet Spot for $58 (2024-04-08); Amy suggested homemade banana bread (2024-04-08); Crystal confirmed nut-free snacks because Michelle had a mild allergic reaction in 2023 (2024-04-08); star-shaped cookies and blue punch were served at the May 2024 movie night, and leftover cupcakes were donated to a local daycare (2024-05-12).
rollups.topic: Family movie-night snacks and food contributions

rollups.text: Crystal’s family movie-watching count: on May 15, 2024, Crystal said the family had watched 15 family movies in six weeks, 50% more than its initial goal. On April 8, she said the family had completed eight selected movies over the preceding weekend. These are separate reported totals for different periods.

Crystal’s reported family movie-weekend snack budgets changed over time: $50 on March 12, 2024; $65 on March 28; $75 later on March 28; $70 for the May 11–12 marathon; and $85 mentioned for a May 2024 weekend. The records reflect different planning moments and events, rather than one consistently tracked budget.

Crystal’s movie preferences shifted: on March 12, 2024, she sought a mix including adventure, comedy, educational value, and family-friendly films. On April 8, after a family movie marathon, she said her preference for family-weekend viewing had shifted toward animated musicals and away from action-heavy films. By May 15, she also sought family films with educational value and cultural significance.

Crystal’s date-night plans with Thomas at The Harbor Grill developed across multiple occasions. On April 6, 2024, Thomas booked a surprise dinner for Crystal at 7:00 PM to celebrate the start of the movie weekend; Crystal asked for romantic films to watch afterward. On April 20, Crystal planned another date night at The Harbor Grill to celebrate a successful family weekend, but the proposed itinerary was not confirmed. On May 13, Crystal reported that she and Thomas had enjoyed a meal at The Harbor Grill and spent $120, including wine and dessert. On May 15, she again asked for romantic movie recommendations for a planned date night, with no date specified.
rollups.topic: Date nights at The Harbor Grill

rollups.text: Crystal’s family movie-night playlist and music activities: by May 15, 2024, Crystal had added the soundtracks from Coco and Wish to a family playlist of 25 songs, played during breaks and activities. Emily offered to bring a karaoke machine and Christopher volunteered to DJ with a family-friendly playlist for a planned May 2024 gathering; these were discussed as contributions, but the records do not confirm they occurred. Mason’s playlist of 30 songs was also discussed, but its contents and effect on karaoke were not established.
